question: I'm screening outpatient clinic patients with anemia for rheumatologic autoimmunity. Among patients who were followed as outpatients (rather than admitted to the hospital) and who ever had a hemoglobin value below 10 on any lab test, who showed the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein antibody response? Please return, for every patient whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level reached the highest point ever recorded on their lab tests (list all of them if several share that highest level): the patient ID, the patient's sex, and that highest-ever recorded anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level. Nothing else.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein refers to the antibody measured in the laboratory tests (anti-RNP).
gold_sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, MAX(CAST(r.RNP AS REAL)) AS highest_level FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory r ON r.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory h WHERE h.ID = p.ID AND h.HGB < 10) GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX HAVING MAX(CAST(r.RNP AS REAL)) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(r2.RNP AS REAL)) FROM Patient p2 JOIN Laboratory r2 ON r2.ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory h2 WHERE h2.ID = p2.ID AND h2.HGB < 10))

expected.sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, MAX(CAST(r.RNP AS REAL)) AS highest_level FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory r ON r.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory h WHERE h.ID = p.ID AND h.HGB < 10) GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX HAVING MAX(CAST(r.RNP AS REAL)) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(r2.RNP AS REAL)) FROM Patient p2 JOIN Laboratory r2 ON r2.ID = p2.ID WHERE p2.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory h2 WHERE h2.ID = p2.ID AND h2.HGB < 10))
expected.evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein refers to the antibody measured in the laboratory tests (anti-RNP).
